rows.grounds: yāvat (until) + darpaṇa-saṃkāśam (resembling a mirror); expresses the degree to be reached
instrumental of śaivāla (algae/moss), the covering material
chādayet (should cover) + tataḥ (thereafter); fused form kept as one token

items.question: What degree of reflectiveness must be achieved when covering the surface with algae in this procedure?
premises: The wise ritual actor has already spread the prepared powders.
Algae are to be used as the covering material.
The covering must continue until a mirror-like appearance is attained.
items.inference: Therefore, the ritual actor should thereafter cover the surface with algae until it becomes mirror-like.
items.plain_english: Thereafter, one should cover it with algae until it becomes as reflective as a mirror.
